You are reverse-engineering a compiled C++ binary as a BLACK BOX. The binary is at /workspace/dataset/test15_executable.

Invocation contract: it takes EXACTLY 6 positional args: scheme host port path query fragment.
It prints 8 lines to stdout: scheme(), host(), port(), path(), query(), fragment(), to_string(), is_valid().

RULES OF ENGAGEMENT:
- You may ONLY run the binary and observe stdout/stderr/exit code. There is NO C++ source available; do not look for any.
- ALWAYS quote every argument in the shell, including empty ones: /workspace/dataset/test15_executable "http" "example.com" "80" "/" "" ""
- Make output unambiguous. Use a helper that numbers the lines and marks empties, e.g.:
    p(){ printf '### IN: [%s]\n' "$*"; /workspace/dataset/test15_executable "$@" >/tmp/o 2>/tmp/e; printf '  exit=%d\n' $?; nl -ba -s': ' /tmp/o | sed 's/$/<END>/'; if [ -s /tmp/e ]; then echo "  STDERR: $(cat /tmp/e)"; fi; }
  Then call p with 6 quoted args. Beware: trailing empty args are easy to lose — verify your helper really passes 6.
- Run MANY cases (30+ minimum). Batch them into a few Bash calls; do not do one call per case.
- Be exhaustive about the boundary cases in your assigned dimension.
- Do not guess. Every rule you report must be backed by an observed input/output pair you actually ran.

Baseline facts already established (re-verify if relevant to you):
- ("http","example.com","80","/","","")  -> lines: http / example.com / 80 / "/" / "" / "" / "http://example.com:80/" / 1
- ("http","example.com","-1","/","","") -> to_string is "http://example.com/"  (port omitted), port() prints -1
- ("http","example.com","0","/","","")  -> to_string is "http://example.com:0/"  (port 0 IS included)
- ("http","","80","/","","")            -> to_string is "http://:80/", is_valid=1
- ("","example.com","80","/","","")     -> to_string is "/" (scheme+authority both vanish), is_valid=1
- ("","","0","","","")                  -> to_string is "", is_valid=0

Report rules as precise, implementable statements (pseudocode-level), each with the concrete evidence line.


DIMENSION: interactions and whole-URL round-trip behavior that single-field probes would miss.

- Does a "?" or "#" embedded in the PATH arg get re-split into query/fragment by from_components? Test ("http","h","80","/p?x=1#f","","") and inspect lines 4,5,6,7.
- Does a ":" + digits embedded in HOST get split into the port, overriding argv[3]? Test ("http","h:9090","80","/","","").
- Does "user@" in host become userinfo and appear in to_string? Test ("http","u:p@h","80","/","","").
- Does a full URL passed as the scheme arg get parsed? Test ("http://h:80/p?q#f","","-1","","","").
- Combined weirdness: all six fields non-empty and weird at once, e.g. ("HTTPS","EXAMPLE.com","443","/a/../b%20c","b=2&a=1","#top") -> report all 8 lines exactly. This is a key differential test case.
- Idempotence check: take to_string() output of a case, and see if feeding its components back reproduces it.
- Also probe several "realistic" cases to be used later as regression fixtures, and report all 8 lines verbatim for each:
  ("http","example.com","80","/","","") ; ("https","www.google.com","443","/search","q=test","results") ;

input.dimension: Interactions and whole-URL round-trip behavior (cross-field effects, to_string() composition, idempotence, regression fixtures)

rules.rule: to_string() is a pure concatenation with NO re-parsing:  s = scheme.empty() ? "" : (scheme + "://" + host + (port>=0 ? ":"+itoa(port) : ""));  s += path;  if(!query.empty()) s += "?"+query;  if(!fragment.empty()) s += "#"+fragment;  return s;

The ENTIRE authority (host AND the ":port" piece) is emitted only when scheme is non-empty. If scheme=="", both host and port vanish from to_string() even though host()/port() still report them. Full 2x2x2 truth table confirmed.
The "://" separator is emitted unconditionally after a non-empty scheme, even when host is empty and port<0 — producing "scheme://" with nothing after it (and "scheme:///path" when only path is set).
from_components does NOT re-split the PATH argument on '?' or '#'. Embedded '?'/'#' stay inside path(); query() and fragment() remain exactly as passed. This makes to_string() ambiguous/lossy.
A ':'+digits suffix embedded in HOST is NOT split into the port and does not override argv[3]; both appear, yielding a double colon-port in to_string().
"user:pass@" in HOST is NOT extracted as userinfo; the whole string is stored as host() verbatim and pasted before the ":port".
A full URL passed as the SCHEME argument is NOT parsed. It is only ASCII-lowercased and then has a literal "://" appended; host/path/query/fragment stay empty and is_valid()=0.

PATH normalization (the only structural mutation): if path is non-empty and path[0] != '/', a single '/' is prepended. Empty path stays empty. No other rewriting (no dot-segment collapsing, no '//' collapsing, no trimming, no percent re-coding).
SCHEME is ASCII-lowercased byte-wise, with no trimming, no validation, and no character filtering. HOST is never case-folded. Query/fragment never case-folded.

QUERY and FRAGMENT are stored byte-verbatim and prefixed with a literal '?' / '#' only when non-empty — a leading '?' in query or leading '#' in fragment is duplicated, and a '#' inside query is emitted raw.
is_valid() == (!host.empty() || !path.empty()) — evaluated after the path '/' -prepend. It is completely independent of scheme, port, query and fragment.

rules.rule: PORT: value = std::stoi(argv[3]) (leading whitespace/sign allowed, stops at first non-digit); then it is kept only if 0 <= v <= 65535, otherwise it is stored as -1. port() prints the stored value; to_string() includes ":port" iff port >= 0 (so 0 IS printed).

PORT parse failures are fatal (uncaught exception -> SIGABRT, exit 134, nothing on stdout): non-numeric argv[3] and EMPTY argv[3] throw std::invalid_argument; argv[3] numerically above INT_MAX throws std::out_of_range.

uncertainties: No string-parsing entry point is reachable through this CLI (all 6 args are components), so I could not test whether a from_string()/parse() function exists that WOULD split host:port, userinfo, or path?query#fragment. All 'no re-split' rules are statements about the from_components path only.

Idempotence was verified at the COMPONENT level (feed lines 1-6 back in). I could not verify string-level round-trip (feed line 7 back in) because there is no way to hand the binary a whole URL string; the observed to_string() is provably non-injective, so a string round-trip could not be lossless in general.
Scheme lowercasing looked byte-wise ASCII-only (ÄÖÜ unchanged, run under the container's default locale). Behavior under a different LC_ALL/LC_CTYPE was not tested.

Exact stoi acceptance grammar was inferred from samples (" 80"->80, "+80"->80, "0x50"->0, "1e3"->1, "007"->7); I did not enumerate every whitespace form (e.g. leading tab/newline) or unusual sign combinations.

Whether the port clamp is written as `if (p < 0 || p > 65535) p = -1` versus an unsigned-range check cannot be distinguished; both fit all observations (every out-of-range input, positive or negative, yields exactly -1).
The <6-arg case prints nothing at all to stdout or stderr and returns 1; I could not determine whether a usage message goes somewhere else (e.g. it may simply be absent).
Fields containing NUL bytes could not be tested (shell/execve limitation).
Not tested: extremely large inputs near ARG_MAX, or whether any allocation failure path changes behavior.
